scenes.title: Find custom maps and start an indoor map

captions.text: From Mapping, open Custom Maps and select New Custom Map.
The list separates Indoor, Outdoor, Event and Custom maps.
Choose Indoor for this exercise.
Enter a recognizable Name and Description so administrators
can identify the intended site.
Here we use a fictional community coordination centre.
A custom map gives your team a place to keep a floor-plan
image and named areas together.

scenes.title: Draw the site bounds and save the map

captions.text: Scroll to Draw Bounds.
Use the Draw Rectangle tool, choose one corner and then the opposite corner.
The completed blue rectangle shows the extent prepared for the map.
The page also explains that clicking the map sets its centre.
Use accurate boundaries for your own site; this software exercise
uses a fictional schematic.
Select Save,
then check the returned row for the intended name and Indoor type.

scenes.title: Prepare a floor layer and select its image

captions.text: Select Layers on the saved map.
Give the layer a clear Layer Name, keep Order at zero for this first floor,
and choose Floor Plan as its Type.
Under Layer Image, use Choose File to select the training floor-plan image.
The page notes that images larger than two thousand forty-eight
required_labels: Images larger than 2048px will be automatically tiled.

captions.text: pixels are automatically tiled.
Our smaller image keeps this example focused on an ordinary floor-plan upload.

scenes.title: Verify the saved floor and rendered plan

captions.text: Select Add Layer.
Check the saved row rather than assuming the file was accepted.
It shows the ground floor, FloorPlan, Yes under Has Image, and No under Tiled.
Open Region Editor.
Wait for the actual floor image to render and zoom until the rooms are readable.
The schematic contains a briefing room, training room, equipment store
and other fictional team spaces.

scenes.title: Draw a room and complete its properties

captions.text: Use Draw Rectangle in Region Editor to outline the briefing room.
When the shape is complete, Region Properties opens beside the plan.
Enter Briefing area, followed by training, as the Name.
Keep Room as the Type, review Color, and add a short Description.
A useful name connects the drawn boundary to an area people can recognize.
The shape is still prepared until you select Save Region.

scenes.title: Save and reopen the room availability settings

captions.text: This first room has Searchable in dispatch and Dispatchable checked.
Review those two choices deliberately, then select Save Region.
After the page reloads, the room appears under Regions with a Dispatchable badge.
Select its boundary on the plan to reopen the saved properties.
Verify the name, Room type and both checked options.
This lesson verifies those saved settings; it does not dispatch an
incident or test a dispatch search.

scenes.title: Change the name, colour and dispatch availability

captions.text: With the saved room selected, change its name to Briefing
room, followed by training.
Choose the teal Color shown in the form.
Leave Searchable in dispatch checked and clear Dispatchable,
then select Save Region.
These changes affect the same saved region.
Before saving, the list can still display the previous name and
badge, so use the returned view to check what actually persisted.

scenes.title: Verify the updated room and its boundary

captions.text: After reload, the boundary is teal, the list has the new Briefing room name,
and the Dispatchable badge is gone.
Select the boundary again.
Region Properties now shows the saved teal Color, Searchable in dispatch
checked, and Dispatchable unchecked.
The floor image and boundary remain in place.
This readback confirms the change beyond the form on which you prepared it.

scenes.title: Reopen the map and check its stored extent

captions.text: Return to the map list and open Edit for the intended map.
The Indoor type, Name and Description are retained.
Scroll to Draw Bounds to see the stored rectangle on the background map.
Check that extent against your own permitted site plan before relying on it.
In this recording the floor image is a fictional schematic, and does
not represent the real buildings shown on the background map.

scenes.title: Use named areas across department types

captions.text: The same workflow can support community paramedicine and mental health
response teams, search-and-rescue organizations, security companies,
wildland contractors, industrial emergency teams, fire and E M S departments.
Keep an appropriate site image, name useful areas, and verify the saved
region settings after each change.
A floor plan and room boundary provide shared location context;
they do not by themselves establish live indoor personnel tracking.
Select the boundary to review Region Properties before the next update.
